source_uncertainties: Unspecified dose, timing or normal findings were not inferred.
Published management is descriptive and requires separate normative review.
Secondary sepsis and antimicrobial hypersensitivity developed after emergency surgery and are not preoperative diagnostic requirements in this MVP.
The combined drain-culture narrative is delayed follow-up and is not released by the time-zero EHR.
ground_truth.benchmark_assessment_scope: Acute presentation through emergency laparotomy and immediate postoperative stabilization. Published later sepsis is a separate source outcome, not required to call the preoperative diagnosis clinically acceptable.

benchmark_target_diagnosis.label: Rupture of continent urinary diversion pouch with intraperitoneal leak
source_locators: PDF pp. 1–2, case presentation and operative confirmation
benchmark_target_diagnosis.rationale: The published secondary sepsis was diagnosed only after surgery; time-zero models cannot observe that later complication.

acceptable_diagnoses.label: Ruptured continent urinary diversion pouch with intraperitoneal leak or peritonitis before later sepsis is established
conditions: Recognizes pouch rupture/leak as the acute cause and arranges urgent source control.
acceptable_diagnoses.reason: The source documents rupture at emergency surgery, while sepsis was diagnosed only after postoperative deterioration.

critical_diagnoses_to_not_miss: Acute urinary reservoir rupture with intraperitoneal leak/peritonitis and need for source control
